title: Keys, S., GitHub, meeus/v3/saturnring/saturnring.go (Go transcription of Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, chapter 45 The Ring of Saturn, MIT)
note: Read in full. Source of the chapter 45 step list as code: the ring-plane inclination and node polynomials, the two-pass light-time loop, the B, B′, ΔU and P formulas, a = 375.35 arcseconds divided by Δ, b = a sin abs(B), and the four inner-edge fractions 0.8801, 0.8599, 0.6650, 0.5486. The book itself was not read, so constants are quoted from this transcription.

note: Read in full. Source of the chapter 46 satellite series as code: time arguments t1 to t11, the Mimas to Iapetus element series, the rotation through 28.0817 and 168.8112 degrees, the D angle, the per-satellite constants K (20947 to 91820) and the factor W = Δ/(Δ + Z/2475).

title: Dourneau, G. (1993). Orbital elements of the eight major satellites of Saturn determined from a fit of their theories of motion to observations from 1886 to 1985. Astronomy and Astrophysics 267, 292-299
note: ADS scan read through OCR. Source of the 22,000 observed coordinates, the element tables (Mimas epoch JD 2411093.0, L0 127.64 degrees, n 381.994497 degrees per day, e 0.01905, t0 1866.39), and the stated uncertainties of 350 to 500 km for satellites II to VI, 800 to 1000 km for Mimas and Iapetus, 2500 km for Hyperion, and 50 to 100 km from the 1980 mutual events.

title: IMCCE and Observatoire de Bordeaux, satel/do87 README: Analytical theory of motion of the eight major Saturnian satellites, G. Dourneau (1987, 1993), dated 2006 March 30
note: Read in full. States that the Fortran subroutines return saturnicentric rectangular coordinates in the FK4 system (B1950.0) and cites the 1987 thesis and the 1993 paper.

title: Harper, D. and Taylor, D. B. (1993). The orbits of the major satellites of Saturn. Astronomy and Astrophysics 268, 326-349
note: ADS scan read through OCR, abstract and Table 2b. Source of the masses, J2 0.016478 and J4 -0.00110 for a 60,000 km reference radius, the equator node 168.8387 and inclination 28.0653 degrees (B1950), and the side-by-side Dourneau values 168.8112 and 28.0817 degrees.

title: Vienne, A. and Duriez, L. (1995). TASS1.6: Ephemerides of the major Saturnian satellites. Astronomy and Astrophysics 297, 588-605
note: ADS scan read through OCR, abstract, sections 1 and 2 and the series tables. Source of the 55 fitted parameters, the elements p, λ, z, ζ, the precision of about ten kilometres, and the fit to about 50,000 equations of condition from the Strugnell and Taylor catalogue.

title: IMCCE and Universite de Lille, satel/tass17 README: TASS 1.7, new version of the TASS theory including Hyperion (A. Vienne and L. Duriez, 1996 November 14)
note: Read in full. Dates TASS 1.7 to 1996 November 5, names the Fortran file tass17.f, and states that positions are saturnicentric, referred to the mean ecliptic and equinox of J2000.0.

title: Lainey, V., Karatekin, O., Desmars, J. et al. (2012). Strong tidal dissipation in Saturn and constraints on Enceladus' thermal state from astrometry. The Astrophysical Journal 752, 14
note: Abstract read from arXiv only. The numerical ephemeris behind NOE-6-2011-MAIN, fitted to more than a century of astrometry, with k2/Q = (2.3 plus or minus 0.7) x 10^-4.

title: Lainey, V., Jacobson, R. A., Tajeddine, R. et al. (2017). New constraints on Saturn's interior from Cassini astrometric data. Icarus 281, 286-296
note: Abstract read from arXiv only. Fit of eight main and four coorbital moons including Cassini astrometry, k2 = 0.390 plus or minus 0.024 and k2/Q = (1.59 plus or minus 0.74) x 10^-4.

title: Lainey, V., Gomez Casajus, L., Fuller, J. et al. (2020). Resonance locking in giant planets indicated by the rapid orbital expansion of Titan. Nature Astronomy 4, 1053-1058
note: Abstract read from arXiv only. Titan migrates outward at 11.3 plus or minus 2.0 cm per year. Cited as the reason that tidal terms belong in a long-span ephemeris.

title: Afigbo, V. M., Hedman, M. M. et al. (2025). Unveiling What Makes Saturn Ring: Quantifying the Amplitudes of Saturn's Planetary Normal-Mode Oscillations and Trends in C-Ring Properties Using Kronoseismology (VII). Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets 130, e2024JE008710

title: Arlot, J.-E. and Thuillot, W. (2008). Predictions of the events of the satellites of Saturn during the 2009 equinox. Astronomy and Astrophysics 485, 293-298
note: Read in full from the HAL PDF. Source of the four event types, TASS and Do93 predictions, 441 events from 2008 Sep 9 to 2010 Jun 18 with 123 easily observable, the 10 to 30 s spread in times of maximum, the 0.1 arcsecond to 600 km scale, the column definitions (TT, penumbral and umbral contacts, flux drop, impact parameter), and the Titan shadow transit window 2009 Feb 24 to 2010 Jan 9.

title: Arlot, J.-E., Emelyanov, N. V., Lainey, V. et al. (2012). Astrometric results of observations of mutual occultations and eclipses of the Saturnian satellites in 2009. Astronomy and Astrophysics 544, A29

title: Arlot, J.-E., Derouazi, Th., Ruatti, Ch., Thuillot, W. (1995). Satellites de Saturne I a VIII : phenomenes et configurations pour 1996. Bureau des longitudes

Source of the event codes Pd, Pf, Od, Of, Ed, Ef, Im, Em, the rule that times refer to the satellite centre, the 14 s to 450 s contact-to-contact durations, the use of Dourneau 1993 and VSOP82, and the 10 to 15 arcsecond reading accuracy of the configuration curves.
